title: Tips on retopo Ai generated 3D models?
author: Conscious_Tension811
selftext:
Currently tackling 3D model & texture for a game i'm building, testing out Tripo and 3dstudioai

Seen mentioned in the sub the topology these tools generates isn't good for animation. I've done a bit of research and now wondering what tools I can use and what outcome I should aim for?

TIA!

replies.author: justifun
replies.body: While it does a great generation of the model and decent textures, the resulting mesh is going to be between 500K and 1M tris.  and not .

replies.author: Rizzlord
replies.body: That's why I have uploaded a tutorial how too reduce it.

comments.author: BaseballOk2157
comments.body: Finding AI meshes convenient but difficult to work out in totality. How do you separate out cloth and hair for example? Means you need to remove the cloth and hair and add them back again. Struggling with some of these things currently

replies.author: corysama
replies.body: Can't find the link now. But, there is a recent photo->mesh generator that can at least break down common objects into component parts as separate meshes. This includes internal, non-visible details like separate drawers inside furniture or joint connectors on the limbs of a toy figurine.

comments.author: Fluid_Cup8329
comments.body:
Oof. I wouldn't even attempt on that mess. 

You'd be better off using them as references on models from scratch. 

Being dead serious, you'll have an awful time trying to fix any of that.

replies.author: Conscious_Tension811
replies.body:
yeah damn i'm kind of figuring this out now. still valuable as a reference i suppose.

let's say you're forced to work with this.. what would you do?

replies.author: Fluid_Cup8329
replies.body:
Personally I have 10+ years experience in blender, so I would put that model in the scene and use it as a direct reference to recreate it from scratch, so I ensure the topo is good from the start. 

A good rule of thumb with topo is making sure you can utilize loop cuts in your model as much as possible. I don't think you'd be able to pull a single full loop cut from any of these models. 

Especially if you intend on animating these, you're gonna want the default pose to be a t pose or similar. That's another thing you'd have an extremely hard time pulling off with these models as they are.

replies.author: ExacoCGI
replies.body: I'd rather just rip some models from Cyberpunk 2077 and work with that, at least the clothing and everything will be separated.

replies.author: Dardranight
replies.body: Lo mejor es considerar los modelos de IA como si fueran modelos de alta, "esculturas" y de ahí pasas a un proceso de modelado común y corriente, osea haces una retopo (topologia desde cero usando box modeling) y haces bake en substance o en marmoset y ya te quedan buenos para animar.
